translationRepairs: When Yougui acceded, he made the Emperor custodian of the Eastern Capital, acting prefect of Kaifeng, and honorary Minister of Works.
When Yougui acceded, he made the Emperor custodian of the Eastern Capital, acting prefect of Kaifeng, and honorary Minister of Education (Situ).
司徒 is Minister of Education in this translation's office system, whereas Minister of Works corresponds to 司空.
On dingchou Yu Jing, acting minister of works and grand counselor, became vice minister of works, then was exiled to Luzhou as marshal for nepotism toward officers.
On dingchou Yu Jing, acting minister of works and grand counselor, became vice minister of works, then was demoted to Laizhou as marshal for nepotism toward officers.
萊州 is Laizhou, not Luzhou. The proposal corrects the place while preserving the demotion described by the sentence.
The court had posted Prince of Fu Youzhang at Xuzhou; Yin refused replacement; an edict stripped his titles, restored the surname Jiang, and sent Youzhang, Niucunjie, Liu Yan, and others against him.

The court had posted Prince of Fu Youzhang at Xuzhou; Yin refused replacement; an edict stripped his titles, restored the surname Jiang, and sent Youzhang, Niu Cunjie, Liu Yan, and others against him.
牛存節 is the personal name Niu Cunjie. The existing English accidentally fuses surname and given name.
Cang and Wei are subordinate; Zhang Jun is commissioner of Xiang."
Chan and Wei are subordinate; Zhang Jun is commissioner of Xiang."
澶州 is Chan Prefecture. Cang would correspond to 滄 and is the wrong place.
This is another fused rendering of 牛存節 and should use the same Niu Cunjie form as the earlier sentence.
(《Zizhi Tongjian》: That first month Xuanyi commissioner Prince of Guangde Jing Quanyu died.)〉
(Zizhi Tongjian: In the first month of the second year, Quanyu, Xuanwu military commissioner, acting director of the Secretariat, and Prince Jing of Guangde, died.)〉
廣德靖王 is Quanyu's posthumous title, Prince Jing of Guangde. The revision also restores 守中書令 and corrects 宣武 from the existing Xuanyi mistranscription.

歐陽史 here is Ouyang Xiu's New History of the Five Dynasties. Calling it a Tang history identifies the cited source incorrectly.
